_comment: Source of truth for this service's entire RabbitMQ topology (event-contract.md). This corrects the stale draft at kart-platform/docs/services/kart-payment-service/message-bus-manifest.json, which incorrectly claimed Payment 'consumes no events' - Payment's own approved requirement-spec.md/architecture.md/event-contract.md all clearly state it consumes OrderCreated asynchronously (that consumption is what actually triggers ChargePayment, per architecture.md's Sync/Async Resolution). PaymentCompleted/PaymentFailed/RefundIssued/ChargebackReceived are all published via this service's own EF Core/PostgreSQL transactional outbox (OutboxRelayHostedService), which retries indefinitely until RabbitMQ is reachable rather than dead-lettering - so, per the same convention used across the platform, published events appear only in publishedEvents, never with a DLQ of their own here (their consumers - Order, Notification, Analytics - each declare their own per-event DLQ in their own manifests, per event-standards.md's 'never a shared/global DLQ' rule). payment.read-model-projection.queue is this service's own internal async pipeline: it self-consumes every event this service just published on payment.exchange to keep the MongoDB denormalized read model (CQRS query side) in sync with the PostgreSQL write side - the user's explicit CQRS requirement, a deliberate deviation from database-design.md's own 'no read model needed' conclusion (see contracts/README.md), following the same 'self-consumed event' shape kart-offer-service already uses for its own CQRS projection.
